source.name: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database, 109P/Swift-Tuttle, solution SB405-CPV-2 (equinox J2000, epoch JD 2450000.5); sizes the whole-orbit path's sampling, the comet's position is the catalogue body's

Global Meteor Network, monthly trajectory summary files (traj_summary_monthly_YYYYMM.txt), IAU shower 7 (PER); Vida et al. 2021, MNRAS 506(4); Vida et al. 2020, MNRAS 491(2); fetched by tools/data/fetch-meteoroid-orbits.mjs; a copy ships under data/stories/perseids/

gmn.ruleNote: Qc is GMN's own maximum convergence angle between stations (column Qc, deg) and the Vgeo sigma is the uncertainty column beside Vgeo (km/s), so the reliable set is Qc at least the angle and sigma at most the fraction of Vgeo.

rule.quote: "requiring a minimum convergence angle of 15 degrees between cameras, ensuring an estimated velocity error of no more than 10% of the nominal value" (the 2025 HDBSCAN paper words it: "a minimum convergence angle of 15° between camera detections to ensure reliable triangulation, ... a velocity error not exceeding 10% of the nominal value"); both apply it to the CAMS v3.0 database; they also drop hyperbolic orbits, which the data file already does

source.name: Peña-Asensio and Sánchez-Lozano 2024, Statistical Equivalence of Metrics for Meteor Dynamical Association, Advances in Space Research, doi 10.1016/j.asr.2024.05.005 (arXiv 2405.03308); and arXiv 2507.01501, Meteoroid stream identification with HDBSCAN

concentration.basis: not a published fit. 20 degrees of mean anomaly either side is about 15 years of the 133-year orbit. Young dust is known to crowd near the parent (the early-1990s Perseid outbursts followed the comet's 1992 return), but no published fraction or width is claimed.

source.name: International Meteor Organization, 2020 Meteor Shower Calendar (IMO_INFO(2-19), ed. J. Rendtel), Perseids: active July 17 - August 24, maximum August 12, 13h to 16h UT (node at solar longitude 140.0 to 140.1, J2000), the traditional broad maximum varying between 2020 August 12 08h and 21h UT; archived copy of imo.net/files/meteor-shower/cal2020.pdf, SHA-256 56927b2d2d312c584fb2c9d84b05bca0ab9d6bcc5356e2edf43c75bb0e739493. The demo's year runs from 21 September 2019 (owner decision, O-024). Peak rate ZHR 100: the American Meteor Society calendar figure, as before (IMO gives 110 in the shower's entry and 100 in its working list). The peak instant (I-027) is the moment the Sun's geometric longitude in the J2000.0 ecliptic and equinox is 140.1 deg, the IAU MDC peak solar longitude (radiant.peakSolarLongitudeDeg), found by bisection on the engine ephemeris with no general precession added: 2020-08-12T15:41:56Z, inside IMO's 13h to 16h UT. The rate profile is the same peakRate and fallOffPerDay about that instant

IAU Meteor Data Center, established meteor showers, Perseids (PER, 7), parameter set AdNo 9 (Jenniskens 2023, Atlas of Earth's Meteor Showers): peak solar longitude 140.1 deg, geocentric radiant RA 47.9, Dec +57.9 deg, J2000
